title: Their Own Record

source.title: DAVID ASMAN: Democrats exploit gas-price pain while ignoring their own record
source.byline: David Asman (FNC since 1997; helped launch FBN in 2007; guest anchor across FNC and FBN)
source.note: published 11-05 13:15 EST (modified 14:34); the 11-05 sweep matched it on 'diesel' (diesel, refiner, crude). Read in full on 11-06 via the cloud fetch (the .print page, complete; the web page truncated) as paragraph reductions, no quotation over ten words. Nine body paragraphs, an opinion column: the pump conceded as the vote's cause in the first sentence, then seven paragraphs on the other party's record (Keystone, a carbon tax, EVs, the IRA), then the peaks as numbers and the holder's $3 claim. Chosen over Fox's 'Hegseth faces bipartisan impeachment threat' page because it is the first RI? page to carry the pump as a number and to name diesel as the fuel 'most in need of right now' — the 11-05 note's gap (the RI corner had the pump only as 'the gasoline'); one Fox per day; my call, flagged

object.label: H1 — the Russian diesel deal (PG01 layer 1): the price leg (H1c) read by the vote from the RI? corner — the pump conceded as the vote's cause in the first sentence ('Democrats won largely on the issue of higher gas prices') and then priced: the Trump peak $4.55 in mid-May 2026 against Obama's $4.55 (May 2011; $6.78 adjusted) and Biden's $5.03 (June 2022; $5.79 adjusted); the holder's claim relayed that gas returns to 'the $3 level seen just before the Iran war' once it ends; the voters 'understandably frustrated' with the holder's 'failed estimates' of when the war would end; oil fell sharply in April when a deal looked likely; 'no one knows when the war will end'. Diesel and jet fuel named as the fuel 'we're in most need of right now', with the shortage routed through a 2021 pipeline cancellation. The deal, Russia, the cargo and the Strait are not on the page; the war is on it in one paragraph

zAxis.pos: prices came down by the deal before the vote, and the vote was not the pump's verdict
zAxis.neg: they did not — the pump peaked at $4.55 in May, the vote went on it, and the cure is dated to a war's end no one can date

transformNote: the shadow is the holder's promise — diesel 'COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST' (10-11) and its clocks. On this page the promise appears in its post-vote form, relayed by the holder's own corner: gas returns to $3 once the war ends, and the war's end is what 'no one knows'. The column's vehicle is the other party's record — Keystone, a carbon fee, the F-150, the IRA — and it adjusts two of three peaks for inflation and not the third. The clocks are conceded from the RI corner for the first time in the column's own voice: the holder's estimates were 'failed', and the voters' frustration with them 'understandable'. The column does not say what the deal was for

lines.quote: Democrats exploit gas-price pain while ignoring their own record; they are in no position to criticize current gas prices
lines.note: THE DOOR (hed + dek): 'gas-price pain' conceded in the hed as the thing the other party ran on; the vehicle is the other party's record. The HTML title is different ('Democrats accused of raising gas prices through energy policy moves')
lines.zWhy: gas-price pain named in the hed is the price's verdict conceded

lines.quote: the incredible irony of this election: Democrats won largely on the issue of higher gas prices — and have done everything they could to raise gas prices when in power
lines.note: THE CONCESSION: the vote read as the pump's verdict in the first sentence — the RI corner's clearest statement of the predicate — then the subject changed; 'irony' the vehicle
lines.zWhy: an election won largely on higher gas prices is the price's verdict, from the holder's corner

lines.quote: Biden's first executive order cancelled Keystone XL — 1,200 miles, 830,000 barrels a day of Canadian heavy sour crude for Gulf Coast refineries built for it, which make diesel and jet fuel, 'exactly the kind of fuel we're in most need of right now'
lines.note: THE DIESEL LINE from the RI corner: the shortage named and dated to now, its cause routed through a 2021 cancellation — a mechanism with the right fuel and the wrong date
lines.zWhy: diesel named as the fuel most needed now is the deal's object conceded short

lines.quote: Obama vetoed the Keystone XL Pipeline Approval Act on February 24, 2015; the Senate's override failed March 4, 2015
lines.note: a dated record line about a different decade — right domain, wrong plane
lines.zWhy: a 2015 veto reads neither way on the 2026 pump

lines.quote: other Democratic contenders favour a carbon tax that would raise gas prices at once: Harris on Sept. 4, 2019, 'there will be a carbon fee'; Buttigieg campaigned for one
lines.note: the 2019 primary as evidence on the 2026 pump — surface-bound
lines.zWhy: a 2019 carbon-fee pledge reads neither way on the 2026 pump

lines.quote: Buttigieg pushed automakers toward EVs consumers were not buying; GM absorbed $11.2 billion in losses; Ford dropped the electric F-150 Biden test-drove in Dearborn in May 2021 and took a $19.5 billion write-down; EVs failed in a Chicago winter
lines.note: the EV paragraph — figures without sources, none of them on the pump; surface-bound
lines.zWhy: EV write-downs read neither way on the 2026 pump

lines.quote: the Green New Deal folded into the 'Inflation Reduction Act' — a 'multi-trillion-dollar green energy spending boondoggle' and a major factor in the Biden administration's 21.5% cumulative inflation, 'which Democrats blame on Trump'
lines.note: the page's highest line: 'boondoggle' the vehicle; the inflation figure unsourced; the blame reassigned across administrations
lines.zWhy: a prior administration's inflation reads neither way on the 2026 pump, slightly toward the verdict denied

lines.quote: the peaks: Obama $4.55 a gallon 'in some areas' in May 2011 ($6.78 today), Biden $5.03 in June 2022 ($5.79 today), Trump's highest $4.55 in mid-May this year
lines.note: THE PUMP AS A NUMBER FROM THE RI CORNER, for the first time on the Press: three peaks, two of them inflation-adjusted and the third not; 'dwarf' the vehicle
lines.zWhy: a $4.55 peak in May of this year is the price's path conceded, with the comparison doing the work

lines.quote: gas will return to the $3 level seen just before the Iran war once it ends
lines.note: constitutive — THE PROMISE IN ITS POST-VOTE FORM, relayed by the holder's corner: the cure conditional on the war's end, undated. Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: voters 'became understandably frustrated with the president's failed estimates' of when the war would end; oil dropped sharply in April when a deal looked likely; 'no one knows when the war will end'
lines.note: THE CLOCKS CONCEDED FROM THE RI CORNER: the holder's estimates called failed in the column's own voice, the April dip dated, the cure's date declared unknown — the page's most fluid line, and its one challenge predicate
lines.zWhy: estimates of the war's end called failed by the holder's own corner is the cure undated

lines.quote: Democrats are in no position to criticize current gas prices given their record
lines.note: the close: the verdict conceded again by implication ('current gas prices') and the subject changed again
lines.zWhy: a close that disputes who may criticize the price concedes the price
